capital: The largest pile of people in the realm, and they all know it.
Where the laws are written, ignored, and then written again, angrier.
town: A market, a temple, and a grudge that goes back four generations.
Prosperous enough for two taverns, which is two too many for the priest.
Everyone here is related. Nobody will say how.
village: Eleven houses and a well that everyone is politely lying about.
The kind of place that has one road and uses it mostly for leaving.
A hamlet with a scarecrow the locals nod to.
castle: Fortified against an enemy that stopped existing a century ago.
Somebody's ancestral seat. Somebody's, anyway. It changes hands often.
dungeon: The stairs go down further than the hill is tall. Nobody wants to discuss this.
Sealed by royal decree. The seal is on the inside.
Three expeditions went in. Two came out. Neither of them was the second one.
cave: A hole. A committed, ambitious hole.
Something is breathing in there, and it is doing it on purpose.
The local children dare each other to the entrance and no further.
ruin: Stones arranged by people who had better tools than you and still lost.
The architecture is beautiful. The reason it is empty is not.
Somebody put a great deal of work into this and then something happened.
tower: One room per floor. Each floor is worse than the one below it.
Built by a wizard with something to prove and no planning permission.
It is taller on the inside. That is not a metaphor.
shrine: A god nobody remembers, still accepting offerings out of habit.
The altar is cracked and the crack is the important part.
Pilgrims come here to ask for things. The answers are technically yes.
camp: Tents, a fire, and a very specific silence when strangers arrive.
Somebody is cooking. Somebody is always cooking. Nobody is eating.
oddity: There is no good word for what is going on here.
A door standing in a field, hinged to nothing, firmly shut.
The grass grows in a perfect circle and the birds route around it.

dungeon: They say the bottom floor is furnished. Furnished, mind. Curtains and everything.
A fellow went in with forty men and came out with a very good soup recipe.
ruin: My grandmother's grandmother saw the lights there. She said they waved.
Take nothing from a ruin. Or take everything. Half measures are what get you.
tower: The wizard's still up there. Been up there since before the war. Not once come down.
Knock three times and it opens. Knock four and you're the one who answers.
oddity: Don't go. Don't. I'm not going to explain, because I can't.
It moved last spring. Two fields east. Nobody talks about it at market.

hitFlavor: {A} {V} {T} — {D}. That will bruise in a shape.
{T} takes {D} and does not enjoy it.
{A} {V} {T} for {D}. Somewhere, a bard is already lying about this.
critFlavor: {A} {V} {T} for an unreasonable {D}. Everyone present feels it.
{D}. {T} was not built for that and now demonstrably is not.
{A} {V} {T} for {D}. That was the good one.
A perfect {V}. {D} damage. {T} briefly leaves the ground.
missFlavor: {A} swings at {T} and hits the concept of air.
{A} misses {T} entirely and has to live with that.
{T} is simply not where {A} committed to.
{A} whiffs. {T} does not even do it the courtesy of dodging.
deathFlavor: {T} falls over and stays that way.
{T} goes down without ceremony, which is the only dignified way to do it.
{T} is defeated, and looks faintly relieved about it.
levelFlavor: Level {L}. You feel marginally harder to kill.
Level {L}. Something in your back stops hurting and something else starts.
Level {L}. You have gotten better at this, which is a worrying sentence.
Level {L}. The universe files an updated assessment of you.
idleFlavor: The wind carries something that is nearly a voice.
A crow watches you from a fence post and takes notes.
Somewhere behind you, something decides not to.
The road goes on. It is not in a hurry and neither, apparently, are you.
You smell rain, or a fire, or a very confident animal.
For a moment the whole world sounds like it is holding its breath.
npcLine: "You want my advice? Don't go east. Or do. I'm not your mother."
"They found another one in the well. Same as the last. Same exactly."
"I'd sell you something, but you've got the look of a person who haggles."
"My husband went into the woods for firewood. That was in spring. We have plenty of firewood."
"Don't trust the priest. Don't trust the miller. Trust the goat."
"Everyone says adventurer like it's a job. It's a diagnosis."
"I've seen four of you this month. I've seen one of you come back."
"There's coin in monster parts, if you're not squeamish and not particular."
"You'll want a better sword. You'll want a better everything, frankly."
"Ask me about the tower. Go on. Ask me. ...No, I've changed my mind."
"My cousin was eaten by something with opinions. He'd have hated that."
"Gods are real, they're just not very good at their jobs."
"If a door in a field is shut, friend, leave it shut."
signText: NO ENTRY. THIS MEANS YOU. YES, YOU SPECIFICALLY.
Beware of the dog. The dog is fine. Beware of what the dog is afraid of.
Lost: one sword, sentimental value, answers to 'Gerald'.
By order of the Crown, this place does not exist. Please do not tell it.
Free to a good home. Or any home. Please.
Trespassers will be prosecuted. Survivors will be prosecuted twice.
The bridge toll is one coin or one secret. Exact change appreciated.
Here lies nobody. We checked. Twice.
Do not read the next sign.

ask: "I need {N} {I}. Don't ask what for. Actually do ask, later, when I've had a drink."
"Bring me {N} {I} and I'll make it worth your while. Modestly worth. Let's not oversell it."
"{N} {I}. That's the order. My supplier was eaten, which is the third time this year."
nag: "Still {N} {I}. The number has not changed. I would have mentioned."
"{I}. {N} of them. I'm not going anywhere, worse luck."
thank: "All {N}. You actually did it. I had a whole speech ready for if you didn't."
"Lovely. Don't tell me where you got them. I mean it. Don't."

ask: "There's {M} out there. {N} of them, ideally fewer by supper."
"Kill {N} {M}. I'd do it myself but I've got a bad back and a good excuse."
"{N} {M}. They've been at the livestock, the washing, and once at my aunt."
nag: "{M}. {N} of them. They are not culling themselves, which we tried."
"Still out there, then. The {M}. I can hear them from here."
thank: "That's the {M} dealt with. The village will be insufferable about it for weeks."
"Done? Properly done? Right. I'll stop flinching at noises."

ask: "Somebody needs to go into {P} and put a stop to whatever is in there."
"{P}. Nobody's come back from it. That's not a warning, that's a job opening."
"Clear out {P}. My brother went in. I'd like the place emptied and, if convenient, him back."
nag: "{P} is still there. Still full. Still nobody's problem but yours, apparently."
"Have you been to {P} yet? No? It hasn't improved."
thank: "{P} is quiet. First time in years. Feels wrong, honestly."
"You went in and came out. That puts you ahead of everyone else who tried."

ask: "Take this to {P}. Don't open it. Don't shake it. Don't listen to it."
"A parcel for {P}. It's paid for. It's mostly legal. It's definitely paid for."
"Get this to {P} before it goes off. I won't define 'off'."
nag: "{P}. The parcel. It is not improving in your bag."
thank: "It arrived. Nobody's shouting. That's the best outcome I'd planned for."
"Delivered, and you didn't open it. I can tell. You'd be different if you had."
